title: 45th sitting of the 20th Majlis
summary: The sitting opened at 9:02 with the Speaker presiding. The government's bill to amend the Penal Code (Law 9/2014), sponsored by Hussain Riza Adam, had its first reading. The rest of this part is the preliminary debate on the bill amending the Political Parties Act (Law 4/2013), which would change how parties register and are funded and raise fines for parties. Most members who spoke supported it; a few questioned the funding formula and the size of the fines, and several exchanges moved to wider arguments about past governments, the Aasandha health scheme and prices. The debate was still going when this part ended. A member's speech carried over from the previous part ends the morning debate on the bill amending the Political Parties Act, with MPs split on how much state money parties should get and whether parties are accountable for members' offences. After a midday break the sitting moves to the government bill amending the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, which would have the President send nominees for the commission's chair and deputy chair to the Majlis. Government-side members back it as a way to make the commission work, while MDP members argue it concentrates power with the President. No vote was held and the Speaker closed the sitting, with the next one set for Tuesday 5 November 2024 at 9:00.

items.title: Opening prayers and start of the sitting
Attendance of members
items.outcome: 40 present, 7 on leave, 4 on official travel as announced

items.title: Announcement of the day's agenda (agenda no. 2024/45)
First reading of the bill to amend the Penal Code (Law 9/2014), submitted by the government through Hussain Riza Adam
Preliminary debate on the bill to amend the Political Parties Act (Law 4/2013), sponsored by Abdul Latheef Mohamed
items.outcome: debated; still continuing at the end of this part

items.title: Preliminary debate on the bill to amend the Political Parties Act (Act 4/2013), sponsored for the government by the member for Dhiddhoo
items.outcome: debated; no vote in this part; paused for the midday break at 11:58

items.title: Continued debate on the bill to amend the Anti-Corruption Commission Act (Act 13/2008), sponsored for the government by the member for Felidhoo (4 hours allotted)
items.outcome: debated; no vote taken; sitting closed before the debate finished

speakers.name: Mohamed Ismail
positions: Raised a point of order asking that claims made in the chamber be accurate.
Supported the bill and reviewed how parties were run under earlier governments.
Supported the bill, saying earlier commissions did not recover money lost to cases such as FPID and MMPRC, and that change is needed.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Supported the amendments and said parties have been run poorly in the past.
Raised a point of order saying false statements in the chamber should be corrected.
Replied to the Vaikaradhoo member, saying democracy means the majority decides, and backed the bill citing the MDP-era record on state debt.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Said state funding for parties is acceptable but the fines in the bill are not.
Criticised the government on Aasandha, taxes and prices.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Supported funding from state revenue but asked for a system to monitor parties, recalling a past Supreme Court ruling on party rules.
Argued the bill gives the President lasting influence over the commission, and that the law will outlive the current President.
Said the Majlis effectively follows the President's wishes; the Speaker corrected him that the Speaker is elected by the MPs.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: On the parties bill, said parties should be judged on what they delivered for livelihoods and questioned a minimum-membership register kept by the Elections Commission.
Argued benefits given to former presidents should be reviewed and that stirring public anger against governments should be stopped lawfully.
On the anti-corruption bill, called it a small amendment that empowers voters through the Majlis, and said many corruption cases remain unresolved.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Questioned the 0.1% funding formula and the sudden rise in fines, and said more parties give voters more choice.
Criticised recent changes to the Aasandha health scheme.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Muhammad
positions: Supported the bill and argued party activity should be regulated, citing past unrest and damage to property.
Supported the bill, saying opposition fears about it are overstated and that Majlis votes provide a check on the President's nominees.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Supported the bill but opposed requiring 10,000 members before a party can receive state funding.
Supported the bill, said the commission failed to act on past corruption claims, and urged recovery of state money and action on suspects.

speakers.name: Abdulla Shareef
positions: Supported the bill, saying public funding strengthens party democracy and fines are justified by parties' debts to state companies.
Supported the bill, said it does not give the President sole power since the Majlis approves nominees, and cited the Civil Service Commission as precedent.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Raised concern that a party can be heavily penalised for offences by one member, and that power is being concentrated in one place.
Argued the Majlis already has a committee that could vet and choose commission heads, and questioned why the bill is being moved so fast.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Supported the Political Parties Act changes and explained how the funding share of 0.1% or 0.2% of state revenue would work out for parties.
Supported the anti-corruption bill, saying nominations vetted by the Majlis are more open than the current process, and pointed to past graft cases.

speakers.name: Abdul Latheef Mohamed
positions: As sponsor, said the bill sets clearer rules for how parties are run and funded and asked members to debate and pass it.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Supported the bill, urged parties to cut personal attacks, and suggested parties field a set share of women candidates.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Supported the amendment and said it can be improved further at committee stage.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Supported the bill, saying it lowers parties' reliance on private donors and makes use of state party funds more open.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shahid
positions: Supported the bill and called on the Elections Commission to regulate parties, including a minimum membership period.

speakers.name: Abdulla Rifau
positions: Supported the bill and said it should make parties and people misusing them face fines.

speakers.name: Ahmed Naseer
positions: Supported the bill and reviewed how parties were run from 2004, arguing party money should serve the country.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: Supported the bill, suggested funding be split by membership and election results, and backed the fines.

speakers.name: Mohamed Mamdooh
positions: Supported the bill, saying it rebuilds public trust and makes party spending accountable.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Supported the bill, including the change to the registration form and the section on contesting after a primary.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Supported the bill, saying the commission has produced few results for years and needs reform, and defended the President's role as the intent to fix this.

speakers.name: Mohamed Afoo Hamid
positions: Supported the bill, citing the commission's 2023 report: 1,151 complaints, 742 cases logged, 40 sent for prosecution and little money recovered.

decisions: Agenda no. 2024/45 was announced and the sitting proceeded.
The Penal Code (Law 9/2014) amendment bill was given its first reading.
The sitting recessed from 10:29 to 11:02 and resumed the preliminary debate on the Political Parties Act amendment bill.
The sitting paused for the midday break from 11:58 to 13:00 and resumed with agenda item 7.
No vote was held on either bill in this part; debate on the Anti-Corruption Commission Act amendment was left unfinished.
The Speaker closed the sitting and announced the next sitting for Tuesday 5 November 2024 at 9:00.
